name: Bankr
rootCause: The AI-powered crypto trading agent platform Bankr on the Base network suffered a social engineering attack. The attacker exploited prompt injection techniques targeting the automated agent trust layer between Grok and Bankrbot — including malicious inputs such as Morse code — to trick the system into executing unauthorized transaction signatures, ultimately gaining access to 14 user wallets and transferring funds. Bankr has suspended the affected functionality, launched an investigation, and pledged to fully reimburse all losses from its treasury.

descriptions.text: The AI-powered crypto trading agent platform Bankr on the Base network suffered a social engineering attack. The attacker exploited prompt injection techniques targeting the automated agent trust layer between Grok and Bankrbot — including malicious inputs such as Morse code — to trick the system into executing unauthorized transaction signatures, ultimately gaining access to 14 user wallets and transferring funds. Bankr has suspended the affected functionality, launched an investigation, and pledged to fully reimburse all losses from its treasury.

Bankr was listed as an incident on Base for 2026-05-19, with the public record attributing about $170,000 in losses to a compromised session key. The supported cause is a session key compromise. The available record does not identify how the key was exposed or whether the exposure came from the frontend, backend infrastructure, a browser session, or another trust boundary.
